reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Evidence suggests target engagement occurred - T-cell expansion was observed with Cmax levels of ~155K copies/μg DNA in monotherapy and ~127K in combination, indicating the engineered T-cells were present and expanding. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: T-cell expansion occurred with different kinetics between arms (median Tmax 3 days monotherapy vs 7.9 days combination), suggesting biological activity. However, the presence of cytokine release syndrome indicates immune activation but may also suggest off-target effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Complete failure at clinical endpoint - 0% ORR in both arms despite evidence of T-cell expansion and immune activation. This suggests the expanded T-cells either could not effectively recognize/eliminate tumor cells or the tumor microenvironment prevented efficacy. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but the universal lack of response across all patients suggests either wrong target selection or inadequate T-cell function in the tumor microenvironment. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Severe toxicity profile (Grade 4 AEs in 5/7 monotherapy patients, 1 death) may have limited dosing or duration, but this appears secondary to the complete lack of efficacy signal.
